questions.q: What were Moses and Aaron to conduct?
questions.a: Moses and Aaron were to conduct a census of the male descendants of Kohath from among the Levites who were 30 to 50 years old.

questions.q: What were the descendants of Kohath to do to serve in the tent of meeting?
questions.a: They were to take care of the most holy things in the tent of meeting.

questions.q: What were Aaron and his sons to take down when the camp set out?
questions.a: They were to take down the curtain that blocks off the Most Holy Place and cover the Box of the Testimony with it. Then they were to cover the Box with porpoise skin, spread a completely blue cloth over the skin, and set its poles in place.

questions.q: Over what were Aaron and his sons to spread a blue cloth, and what were they to put on the cloth?
questions.a: They were to spread a blue cloth over the table. Then they were to put the dishes and the palm-sized bowls and the bowls and the pitchers for the drink offering on it.

questions.q: What was always to be on the table?
questions.a: The bread was always to be on the table.

questions.q: What were they to use after that to cover the table and the things on it, and what were they to set in place to carry the table?
questions.a: They were to spread a scarlet cloth over the table and the things on it and cover that with porpoise skin. Then they were to set the table’s poles in place.

questions.q: How were they to prepare the lampstand and all its equipment for moving?
questions.a: They were to cover the lampstand, its lamps, its tongs, its trays, and all its oil vessels with a blue cloth. Then they were to put the lampstand and all its equipment into a porpoise skin covering and put them on the carrying pole.

questions.q: How was the gold altar to be prepared for moving?
questions.a: They were to spread a blue cloth over the gold altar, cover it with porpoise skin, and set its poles in place.

questions.q: How was all the equipment for the work in the holy place to be prepared?
questions.a: They were to take all the equipment for the work in the holy place and put it into a blue cloth. Then they were to cover it with porpoise skin and put it on the carrying pole.

questions.q: What were they to remove from the altar, and what were they to spread over it?
questions.a: They were to remove the ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.

questions.q: Where were they to put all the equipment that they used at the altar?
questions.a: They were to put all the equipment, including the trays, the meat forks, the shovels, and the basins, on the altar.

questions.q: With what were they to cover the altar before they set its poles in place?
questions.a: They were to cover the altar with porpoise skin before they set its poles in place.

questions.q: Who was to come and carry the holy place and all its equipment after Aaron and his sons finished covering them when the camp set out?
questions.a: The descendants of Kohath were to come and carry them, but they must not touch the holy place, or they would die.

questions.q: Of what was Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, in charge?
questions.a: He was in charge of the oil for the light, the incense of spices, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil. He was also in charge of the whole Dwelling and everything in it, including the holy place and its equipment.

questions.q: What were Moses and Aaron not to do to the Kohathite clans, so that the Kohathites would live and not die?
questions.a: They were not to cause the Kohathite clans to die among the Levites. Aaron and his sons were to assign each man his service and what he must carry.

questions.q: What did Yahweh warn that the Kohathites must not go in to see, or they would die?
questions.a: They must not go in to see the holy place, even for a moment, or they would die.

questions.q: Who alone was allowed to go into the holy place?
questions.a: Only Aaron and his sons were allowed to go into the holy place.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses to do concerning the men of the Gershon clans who would serve in the tent of meeting?
questions.a: Moses was to count the men of the Gershon clans who were 30 years old to 50 years old.

questions.q: What was the work of the Gershonites?
questions.a: The work of the Gershonites was to carry the curtains of the Dwelling and the tent of meeting, its covering, the porpoise skin covering over it, and the curtain at the entrance of the tent of meeting. They were also to carry the hangings of the courtyard, the curtain at the entrance of the courtyard, their ropes, and all the equipment for their service.

questions.q: Who was to direct all the service of the Gershonites, who were under the care of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest?
questions.a: Aaron and his sons were to direct all the service of the Gershonites.

questions.q: Which men of the Merari clans did Yahweh tell Moses to count?
questions.a: Moses was to count the men of the Merari clans who were 30 to 50 years old and who came to serve in the tent of meeting.

questions.q: What were the Merari clans to do in their service for the tent of meeting?
questions.a: They were to carry the frames of the Dwelling, its crossbars, its pillars, and its bases. They were also to carry the pillars of the courtyard with their bases, pegs, and ropes. Moses was to count by name the equipment that each man must carry.

questions.q: Who was in charge of the Merari clans as they served in the tent of meeting?
questions.a: Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest, was in charge of them.

questions.q: What did Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel do to obey Yahweh?
questions.a: They counted the Kohathites by their clans and families, all the men who were 30 to 50 years old and who came to serve in the tent of meeting.

questions.q: How many men of the Kohathite clans did Moses and Aaron count?
questions.a: They counted 2,750 men.

questions.q: How many men of the Gershonite clans did Moses and Aaron count?
questions.a: They counted 2,630 men.

questions.q: Who else was counted in their clans from 30 to 50 years old?
questions.a: The descendants of Gershon were counted in their clans.

questions.q: Who else did Moses and Aaron count in their clans from 30 to 50 years old?
questions.a: The descendants of Merari were counted in their clans.

questions.q: Who counted the Levites according to their clans and families?
questions.a: Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel counted them.

questions.q: When Moses counted each Levite in the clans who was 30 to 50 years old, which men did he count?
questions.a: He counted every man who came to do the work of service and the work of carrying burdens in the tent of meeting.

questions.q: How many Levites did Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel count in total?
questions.a: They counted 8,580 men.

questions.q: When Moses counted each man and kept count of each man’s type of work and responsibility, whom did he obey?
questions.a: When Moses counted each man and kept count of each man’s type of work and responsibility, he obeyed Yahweh.

commentary.text: The duties of the Gershonites and Merarites.
The numbers of the serviceable Levites.

Verses 1–3 The middle-aged men of the tribe of Levi, all from thirty years old to fifty, were to be employed in the service of the tabernacle. The service of God requires the best of our strength, and the prime portion of our time, which cannot be better spent than to the honour of Him who is the First and Best. And the service of God should be done when we are most lively and active. Those do not consider this who put off repentance to old age, and so leave the best work to be done in the worst time.

The Kohathites were to carry the holy things of the tabernacle. All the holy things were to be covered; not only for security and respect, but to keep them from being seen. This not only marked the reverence due to holy things, but the mystery of the things signified by those types, and the darkness of the dispensation. But now, through Christ, the case is altered, and we are encouraged to come boldly to the throne of grace.

We have here the charge of the other two families of the Levites, which, though not so honourable as the first, yet was necessary, and to be done regularly. All the things were delivered them by name. It intimates the care God takes of his church and every member of it. The death of the saints is represented as the taking down of the tabernacle, 2Co 5:1, and the putting it off, 2Pe 1:14. All shall be raised up in the great day, when these vile bodies shall be made like the glorious body of Jesus Christ, and so shall be for ever with the Lord.

God so ordered it, that though the Merarites were the fewest in number, yet they should have most able men among them; for whatever service God calls men to, he will furnish them for it, give strength in proportion to the work, and grace sufficient. The least of the tribes had many more able men than the Levites: those who engage in the service of this world, are many more than those devoted to the service of God. May our souls be wholly devoted to his service.
